allOf.description: Request to create a new template

name.description:
Template display name (optional). When omitted or blank, a name is generated from the template's
content. It can be changed afterwards with PUT /v3/templates/{id}.

category.description: Template category: MARKETING, UTILITY, AUTHENTICATION (optional, auto-detected if not provided)

language.description: Template language code (e.g., en_US) (optional, auto-detected if not provided)

definition.description: Template definition including header, body, footer, and buttons

multiChannel.template: Hello {{0:variable}}! Welcome to {{1:variable}}. We are glad to have you on board.

auto_create_for_sp.description:
Create this template automatically on every sender profile of the organization, now and in future
(default: false). Accepted only from an organization that has been enabled for it, and only at
creation — it cannot be changed afterwards.

submit_for_review.description: Whether to submit the template for review after creation (default: false)

SentDmServicesCommonEntitiesTemplateDefi.description: Complete definition of a message template including header, body, footer, and buttons

header.description: Optional template header with optional variables

body.description: Required template body with content for different channels (multi-channel, SMS-specific, or WhatsApp-specific)

footer.description: Optional template footer with optional variables

buttons.description: Optional list of interactive buttons (e.g., quick replies, URLs, phone numbers)

definitionVersion.description: The version of the template definition format

authenticationConfig.description: Configuration specific to AUTHENTICATION category templates (optional)

SentDmServicesCommonEntitiesTemplateHead.description: Header section of a message template

type.description:
The kind of header. One of:
            
text — up to 60 characters, at most one variable.
image — png, jpg or jpeg. Needs ExampleUrl.
video — mp4. Needs ExampleUrl.
gif — mp4, max 3.5MB. WhatsApp renders larger files as an ordinary video. Needs
ExampleUrl.
document — pdf or docx; only the first page is shown as a thumbnail, so pdf is the
practical choice. Needs ExampleUrl.
location — a map pin, supplied through Location.
            
Kept lowercase because MetaToTemplateConverter writes Meta's format
through ToLowerInvariant() into this field on import, and the two are compared directly.

template.description: The header template text with optional variable placeholders (e.g., "Welcome to {{0:variable}}")

variables.description: List of variables used in the header template

example_url.description:
Request-only. The s.dm URL of the asset Meta's reviewers see — https://s.dm/s/{ID}, eight
uppercase characters, uploaded to s.dm out of band. NormalizeRichHeader
folds it into the synthesized media variable's Props.Sample and clears it, so it never persists
and a stored definition is indistinguishable from an imported one.
            
Stricter than the send path on purpose: TemplateUtils.ValidateMediaVariableValues accepts
any absolute https URL for the per-send asset, because that one is the customer's and may live behind
a signed CDN link. This one is the review sample, has to outlive every resubmission, and so must be
ours. Do not "fix" one to match the other.

static_resource.description:
Whether the asset registered at creation is reused when a caller omits the header's variable at send
time. Default false — the caller must supply it per message, which is the behaviour every
existing template has. Written only when true, so a default-valued header serializes byte-identically
to one imported from Meta.
            
Stored and validated but not yet honoured at send: that lands with the Resumable Upload work,
alongside the code that lets such a template be approved in the first place.

location.description:
Request-only, location headers only. Normalized into the four reserved
LocationVariableNames variables and cleared, for the same reason
as ExampleUrl.

id.description:
The variable's index, and the number its {{index:variable}} placeholder refers to.
            
Omitting it is only safe for a section holding a single variable. The field is a
non-nullable int, so every variable that leaves it out defaults to 0, and a section with two
such variables is refused by the unique-id rule ("variables must have unique IDs"). Number
them from 0 in the order they appear.

name.description:
The variable's name, and the key callers use for it in a send request's parameters object.
Must start with a letter and hold only letters, digits and underscores.

type.description:
One of variable, link or media. Decides which Props fields
are required.

sample.description:
Example value substituted into the template when previewing it and when submitting it to
Meta for review. Free text by nature, so the converter accepts a JSON number or boolean here
and normalizes it — see JsonScalarToStringConverter for why — and guarantees it
is always serialized back out as a JSON string.

SentDmServicesCommonEntitiesTemplateHead.description:
The map pin a location header drops. Meta wants none of this at creation — the component is just
{"type":"header","format":"location"} — so these values exist for Sent: a preview, and the
default a StaticResource header falls back to at send.

SentDmServicesCommonEntitiesTemplateBody.description:
Body section of a message template.
            
A body picks one of two authoring strategies, and mixing them is refused
(TemplateDefinitionValidator.HaveValidChannelConfiguration):
a shared multiChannel body on its own, or
an explicit sms + whatsapp pair, both present.
            
multiChannel together with sms or whatsapp is rejected, and so is
sms or whatsapp on its own — every template is expected to be deliverable on every
channel. rcs is the one true override: it may accompany either strategy to vary the copy,
but cannot stand alone.

multiChannel.description: The shared body, used for every channel. One half of the choice described above.

sms.description: The SMS body. It does not override multiChannel, it replaces it.

whatsapp.description: The WhatsApp body. It does not override multiChannel, it replaces it.

rcs.description:
RCS-specific copy that overrides the chosen strategy for RCS only. The one true override:
optional on top of either strategy, but it cannot be the only body present. Its length cap is
the higher one described on Template.

mms.description:
MMS-specific content — subject, text and attachments.
            
Like Rcs, an override that cannot stand on its own: a template still needs a
MultiChannel body or the Sms + Whatsapp pair to be
deliverable at all. Without this slot MMS renders the shared or SMS body, so it is only needed for
MMS-specific copy, a subject or attachments. When present it replaces that body on MMS rather than
adding to it.

type.description:
The type of body content. Defaults to "text" when omitted, which also fills it in when reading
stored bodies saved without it; the template editor refuses to load a body with no type.

template.description:
The body copy, with variables written as {{index:variable}}.
            
Length cap depends on which channel this body belongs to:
TemplateContentLimits.MaxBodyLength (1024) for multiChannel, sms and
whatsapp — Meta's BODY limit, which a multiChannel body may be delivered under —
and TemplateContentLimits.MaxRcsBodyLength (3072) for an rcs body, which never
reaches Meta. The maxLength advertised on this schema is the 1024 one, because all four
channel bodies share this single schema — an rcs body between the two is accepted.
            
Meta requires every variable to carry surrounding context, so a body is refused unless it also
satisfies all of the following (enforced by TemplateDefinitionValidator):
At least one letter before the first variable and after the last — trailing punctuation
such as "... {{1:variable}}." does not count.
At least (2 × variable count) + 1 words once the placeholders are removed.
No two variables adjacent with only whitespace between them.
No leading or trailing newline, no more than two consecutive line breaks, and no more than
four consecutive spaces.
            
Example: "Hello {{0:variable}}! Welcome to {{1:variable}}. We are glad to have you on
board." — two variables, so at least five words are required, and the copy after the final
variable contains letters.

variables.description: The variables referenced by the body copy, one entry per {{index:variable}} placeholder.

allOf.title: SentDmServicesCommonEntitiesTemplateMmsBodyContent_Properties
allOf.description:
MMS-specific body content.
            
Why MMS needs its own type when the other channels share one: it is the only channel
with a subject line and the only one with attachments. Every other channel's body is text and
variables, which is exactly what TemplateBodyContent already is. Putting
Subject and Media on the shared type instead would give sms, whatsapp and rcs two
members none of them can ever use.
            
Derives from TemplateBodyContent so that every existing consumer of a body slot —
MessageUtils.ConvertVariableToReadable, TemplateDefinition.GetRequiredVariables,
TemplateDefinitionValidator.ApplyBodyContentRules — reads it with no change. The two extra
members are what the MMS strategy and the provider request need on top.

subject.description:
MMS subject line. Optional — most handsets render it above the body, some ignore it entirely.
Deliberately its own field rather than riding TemplateHeader: the header is authored once
and shared across every channel, and carries Meta's 60-character cap plus its no-newline,
no-emoji text rules, none of which describe an MMS subject.

media.description:
Attachments carried by every send on this template, in order. A per-send media_urls on the
request replaces this list rather than adding to it, so a template can hold a default creative and
a caller can still send something recipient-specific.

SentDmServicesCommonEntitiesTemplateMedi.description: One attachment on an MMS template body.

url.description:
Publicly fetchable https URL. The carrier's MMSC fetches this at send time, so it has to
            stay reachable and unauthenticated for the life of the send — including retries and a DLQ
            replay — which is why a presigned URL is not a valid value here.

mediaType.description:
One of MmsMediaTypes. Advisory: the carrier reads the Content-Type off the
            fetched object, not this field. It exists so an authoring UI can render the right preview and so a
            reviewer can see what was intended.

SentDmServicesCommonEntitiesTemplateFoot.description: Footer section of a message template

template.description: The footer template text with optional variable placeholders

variables.description: List of variables used in the footer template

SentDmServicesCommonEntitiesTemplateButt.description: Interactive button in a message template

id.description:
The button's identifier (1-based index), unique within the template.
            
Omitting it is only safe for a template holding a single button. The field is a
non-nullable int, so every button that leaves it out defaults to 0, and two such buttons are
refused by the unique-id rule ("Button IDs must be unique"). Number them from 1 in the order
they should appear — order matters on RCS, where only the first four buttons render.

type.description: The type of button (e.g., QUICK_REPLY, URL, PHONE_NUMBER, VOICE_CALL, COPY_CODE)

props.description: Properties specific to the button type

text.description:
The button's label. Required for every button type, and capped at
TemplateContentLimits.MaxButtonTextLength (25) characters.
            
Meta accepts only static text here, so a label is refused when it contains a
{{...}} variable placeholder, a newline, an emoji, or WhatsApp formatting markup
(*, _, ~) — enforced by ApplyButtonLabelContentRules in
TemplateButtonValidator. Meta reports all four as one error: "Buttons can't have any
variables, newlines, emojis, or formatting characters."
            
AUTHENTICATION OTP buttons are the exception: Meta auto-localizes their label from the
template language, and the converter drops whatever text was sent.

variables.description:
Variables embedded in a dynamic URL button (only when UrlType = dynamic).
Count is capped by TemplateContentLimits.MaxUrlButtonVariables; the placeholder must
appear at the end of Url (validated in TemplateDefinitionValidator).

addSecurityRecommendation.description: Whether to add the security recommendation text: "For your security, do not share this code."

codeExpirationMinutes.description: Code expiration time in minutes (1-90). If set, adds footer: "This code expires in X minutes."

allOf.description: Request to delete a template

delete_from_meta.description: Whether to also delete the template from WhatsApp/Meta (optional, defaults to false)

SentDmServicesEndpointsCustomerAPIv3Shar.description: Standard API response envelope for all v3 endpoints

success.description: Indicates whether the request was successful

meta.description: Metadata about the request and response

SentDmServicesEndpointsCustomerAPIv3Send.description:
A sender profile as the API reports it — the same document the create call accepts, plus the read-only
facts it cannot: each market's status and what it still owes.
            
No status at the profile, brand or campaign level. Brand and campaign are identity, and
identity has no lifecycle. What has one is the registration of a sender in a market, and the approval of
a channel — so status lives there, where it says which specific thing is blocked rather than flattening
several answers into one.

api_key.description:
The API key for this profile.
            
Returned by create and by nothing else. It is shown once; a read that repeated it would
turn every profile list into a credential dump and put the key into any log or cache that keeps a
response body.
            
Omitted rather than null on a read. A key field that is always present and always empty
suggests it could be populated, which is an invitation to populate it; absent says there is nothing
to look for. Doing it with a serializer condition rather than a second response type keeps create and
read on one shape, which is what stops them drifting.

billing.description:
Who pays, reported the way a create would have asked for it: { "inherit": true } for the
organization, { "inherit": false } for the profile, and fallback for the profile drawing on
both.

notifications.description:
Who is notified about this profile's events: ORGANIZATION, SENDER_PROFILE, or
ORGANIZATION_AND_SENDER_PROFILE. Always present — a profile that never chose reports as
ORGANIZATION, the value a create would send to get the default behaviour.

compliance.description:
Brand, campaign, and compliance documents lifted from all SMS markets to the profile root, so a
caller finds everything in one place rather than walking channels.sms[n].compliance.
Per-market compliance is always null in profile responses after the lift.
Absent on a list read (documents are not fetched per market for a list).

SentDmServicesEndpointsCustomerAPIv3Send.description:
Who pays for a sender profile's traffic, as a read reports it.
            
Its own type, field for field the same as
BillingRequest. Same reason as the brand: a response is not
a request, whatever it carries.

inherit.description: Whether the organization pays, rather than the profile.

SentDmServicesCommonChannelsContractsSen.description:
The channels a profile sends on. SMS is a list because a profile can send in several markets; WhatsApp
and RCS are single, because a profile has one business account and one agent.

customer_id.description:
Which customer these channels belong to — the key's own, or the profile named in x-profile-id.
            
Same reason the brand carries one: as the response to /v3/channels there is no other id in
the document, and under x-profile-id this is the profile the call resolved to rather than the
caller. Absent when nested inside a sender profile, whose own id already says whose they are.

mms.description:
The markets this profile can send MMS in, one entry per country, or empty when none.
            
Appears alongside sms rather than replacing an entry in it: the two are separate senders
on the same number and a caller needs to see both — a market can be live for SMS while its MMS row is
still provisioning, or MMS-incapable entirely because the market's sender-type SKU does not carry
it.

voice.description:
The numbers this profile carries phone calls on, one entry per number, or empty when none. Voice is
per number like an SMS market is per country: each number is its own channel row, turned on and off
on its own, and one of them is the line app-originated calls fall back to.

SentDmServicesCommonChannelsContractsSms.description:
One SMS market the profile sends in — its sender, where that sender stands, and what the market wants.
            
A profile may send in several: it is a tenant, not a market. Each carries its own status, because
a profile can be live in one country and mid-registration in another — and each carries what it still owes,
rather than that being reported in a separate array a caller has to join on.

numbers.description:
Every number this market holds or is still owed, each with its area code and its own status
(ACTIVE once it can send, PROVISIONING while it is still to be assigned, INACTIVE once
it could send and no longer can). One entry for a
market holding one number. US 10DLC numbers are assigned when the campaign is approved, so they read as
owed until then. Read-only.

status.description:
Where this market's sender stands, in terms of who is holding it up — PROVISIONING,
ACTION_NEEDED, PENDING_REVIEW or ACTIVE. Read-only.
            
Resolved rather than reported raw: a live sender reads ACTIVE whatever it still owes, a
market with outstanding requirements or an open resubmission request reads ACTION_NEEDED, and a
market that registers with a regime reads PENDING_REVIEW once its brand exists — filing to The
Campaign Registry is ours to do and need not have happened yet, so a dedicated brand created through
this API reads PENDING_REVIEW from the moment it is stored.
            
Describes whether the market can send, not each number: a market holding several numbers reads
ACTIVE as soon as one of them is, whatever the others are doing. Each number's own status is in
numbers.
x-enum-descriptions: We are working on it and there is nothing for you to do — a number is being procured, or a registration is being assembled. Minutes to hours.

**Waiting on you.** Something the market asks for has not been supplied, a regulator rejected what was, or we have asked you to correct and resubmit your identity data. Nothing progresses until you act. For an SMS market, `GET /v3/channels/sms/{country}/{type}` names what it wants and `PATCH` on the same path supplies it — compliance values, documents and numbers alike.

With a regulator or carrier — filed, or assembled and queued for us to file — and their answer is what moves it, to `ACTIVE` or back to `ACTION_NEEDED`. Nothing on your side changes it. Days for SMS, weeks for RCS.
Can carry traffic now. A channel a sender profile runs on its organization's reads `ACTIVE` too — it sends, which is what the field is about.

**It had a working sender and no longer does** — the number was released, or the campaign it carried lapsed. Distinct from `PROVISIONING`, which means it has never sent yet: the same absence of a sender, opposite news. Sends will fail until it returns to `ACTIVE`.

reason_code.description:
Why the market is not ACTIVE, as a stable code: an ErrorCodes CHANNEL_xxx value such
as CHANNEL_001 (something you owe) or CHANNEL_009 (under review). Switch on this rather than
on reason. Omitted while ACTIVE. Read-only; when nothing more specific is known it is the
generic reason for the status.

reason.description:
A sentence for reason_code: this market's own explanation, naming what is outstanding where that
is you. Omitted while ACTIVE.

compliance.description:
What this market has been given. Present on a list read for markets that register (brand and campaign
included, documents absent); fully populated on a single-profile read. Null only when the market
registers with nobody and no compliance data was computed — nothing to show.

SentDmServicesCommonChannelsContractsSms.description: One number of an SMS market.

sender_value.description: The number, or null while it is still to be assigned.

area_code.description:
The number's area code, e.g. 212. While the number is still to be assigned, the area code it was
asked for, or null when it was asked for in any area code.

status.description:
ACTIVE once the number can send; PROVISIONING while it is still to be assigned; INACTIVE
once it could send and no longer can.

campaign_id.description:
The campaign the number is on, or is owed for: the id of its entry in compliance.campaigns.
Omitted for a market that registers no campaigns, and where the campaign is not known — a number recorded
without one, or one owed on a campaign inherited from the organization.

SentDmServicesCommonChannelsContractsSup.description:
What a market has been given: the identity it registers under, its programme, and any documents attached.
            
What it does not carry is what the market asks for. That is the subject of
GET /v3/compliance/requirements, and it is the same answer for every caller — a description of what
a compliance regime wants, not a record of one customer's progress through it. It was reported here as
well for a while, which put the same array in six response shapes and left a caller deciding which of two
sources to believe.
            
Present on a list read for markets that register (carrying brand and campaign), but with
documents absent — documents are not fetched for a list, because a catalog lookup and a document
read per market would multiply across a page. Absent documents is distinct from an empty list:
absent says they were not fetched; empty says the market has been given none. The parent object is null
only when the market registers with nobody and compliance was not computed — nothing to show at all.

brand.description:
The identity this market registers under, with inherit saying whose it is.
            
Reported here rather than on the profile because it belongs to the registration this market
files, and only one market files one. It was a top-level block for a while, which put a per-registration
value beside a list of markets and left a caller to work out which market it belonged to.
            
Absent for a market that registers with nobody — such a market asks for no identity, so there is
none to report. Absent and null mean different things: absent says this market does not ask, null would
say it asks and nothing was supplied.
            
Untyped, like the request side, because its members are declared by the market's own schema rather
than by a C# class. A typed pair here would be a second definition of what a market wants, free to drift
from the one that validates.

campaign.description:
The programme this market registers, with inherit saying whose it is.
            

            
One, not a list. TcrCampaigns permits several and an account built on the admin
side may hold them, but this surface offers one — which is what lets the market's PATCH be an
upsert rather than a collection with an addressable create behind it. An account holding several is
reported as its first and refused on write, rather than half-edited.
            
Carries no id. Nothing addresses a campaign, and an undeclared key would be refused if the
caller sent this object back — which it is meant to be able to do.

campaigns.description:
Every campaign this market registers, each with inherit saying whose it is — oldest first.
            
A list, because a market can now be on more than one. POST
/v3/channels/sms/compliances/US/TEN_DLC/campaigns adds a campaign of the customer's own beside the one it has, and a
profile running on its organization's campaign keeps that one when it adds its own. Campaign
can only show one of them, so it stays as it was, for callers that read it, and this is where the rest
are.
            
The organization's campaign reads "inherit": true and the customer's own read
"inherit": false. Each entry is the shape of Campaign plus id, the campaign's own
id, so several can be told apart. Campaign carries no id, because it is sent back to
PATCH, which refuses a key it does not declare; this list is read-only.
            
Absent for a market that registers with nobody; empty for one that registers and has no campaign
yet.

documents.description:
What has been supplied for this market.
            
Files, not values — the declared halves above carry the values. A document cannot be a JSON value,
so it is sent as multipart on the channel call and reported here as a reference.
            
Absent on a list read, which fetches identity but does not compute compliance documents per
market. Absent and empty mean different things: absent says the documents were not fetched; empty says
the market has been given none.

For an SMS market, `GET /v3/channels/sms/{country}/{type}` names what it wants and `PATCH` on the same path supplies it — compliance values, documents and numbers alike.

With a regulator or carrier — filed, or assembled and queued for us to file — and their answer is what moves it, to `ACTIVE` or back to `ACTION_NEEDED`. Nothing on your side changes it. Days for SMS, weeks for RCS.

An RCS agent as its owner sees it: the order form back, plus where the submission stands.
            
Not RcsSenderResponse. That one is the admin projection and carries the pipeline we
track about a customer's request — internalStatus, statusReason,
isLaunched — and the S3 keys behind the assets. None of that is the customer's to read: an internal

allOf.title: SentDmServicesEndpointsCustomerAPIv3SenderProfilesRequestsCreateSenderProfileRequest_Properties
allOf.description:
Create a sender profile under the authenticated organization.
            
How ownership is expressed. Every capability is one of two things, and the request says
which without a flag per state: { "inherit": true } uses the organization's;
supplying the capability's own fields creates one for the profile; omitting the block entirely means the
profile has none. Ownership is one boolean — data is what owning looks like, and a
second way to say it would let a request contradict itself.

name.description: Display name for the profile. Required.

short_name.description:
Short name, which is also the SMS sender id — required. 3–11 characters of letters, numbers and
spaces, with at least one letter.

billing.description:
Who pays for what this profile sends.
{ "inherit": true } bills the organization; { "inherit": false } (or an empty block) bills
the profile only. Omitting the block bills the profile first, with the organization covering what the
profile's balance cannot. Reads report that default as { "inherit": false }; GET /v3/account
reports it in settings.billing_model.

notifications.description:
Who is notified about this profile's events: ORGANIZATION, SENDER_PROFILE, or
ORGANIZATION_AND_SENDER_PROFILE. Omitting it leaves the profile on the Organization default.

compliance.description:
What this market registers with. Its members are declared by the market itself — call `GET /v3/compliance/requirements?country=&type=` for the authoritative set.

**US `TEN_DLC` is the only market that registers with a regime**, and the only one whose compliance carries `brand` and `campaign`; those are the members described here. Every other market's compliance is document keys, which come from configuration rather than from code and so cannot be listed in this document.

SentDmServicesCommonSenderProfilesContra.description:
Who pays for what a sender profile sends.
            
Ownership reads the same way as BrandRequest and CampaignRequest:
inherit: true is the organization paying; inherit: false (or an empty block) is the
profile paying for itself.
            
An absent block is the one place billing differs from brand and campaign: a profile still has to be
paid for, so omitting billing stores ProfileAndOrganizationBilling — the profile pays first
and its organization covers what the profile's balance cannot (see
ResolveStored). { "name": "..." } stays a complete request.
            
Billing carries no fields of its own yet, so a profile paying for itself is
{ "inherit": false } — or an empty block, which means the same. That is thinner than brand and
campaign, where supplying data is the act of owning; it becomes ordinary the moment billing gains a
contact or a payment method to carry.

inherit.description: Whether the parent organization pays. false is the profile paying for itself.

SentDmServicesEndpointsCustomerAPIv3Send.description:
The channels the profile sends on. Each is independently the profile's own or absent — none can be
inherited, so none carries a mode and presence is the whole of the request.
            
A profile can send SMS in several markets, but create takes one — the market it starts in.
Further markets are added through POST /v3/channels/sms with x-profile-id, and a read returns
them all as a list. Create stays singular permanently rather than being a list that accepts one entry:
the constraint is in the type, and there is no later widening to break the contract.

sms.description:
The market this profile starts sending SMS in — one country and number_type, which is
also what the compliance block is answering for. Omit for a profile with no SMS sender of its
own.

SentDmServicesEndpointsCustomerAPIv3Send.description:
One SMS market a profile sends in — a country and a sender type.
            
A profile may have several. It is a tenant, not a market: a business sending to two countries is
one customer of yours, and forcing it into two profiles would give it two API keys, two inboxes and two
contact lists for one business. The platform already assumes many —
CustomerChannelProviders is unique on (customer, channel, iso, number).
            
No mode: a sender is the profile's own or it has none. Listing a market is the request
for one.
            
Also the discriminator for everything else: the compliance catalog is keyed on (country, number
type), and that pair decides which fields brand accepts and what compliance is asked
for.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country the sender operates in, e.g. US.

number_type.description:
Sender type: LOCAL, MOBILE, TEN_DLC, TOLL_FREE, SHORT_CODE or
ALPHANUMERIC. 10DLC is accepted as a synonym of TEN_DLC. Availability varies
by country.

sender_value.description:
The sender's identity, where the caller chooses it rather than the carrier assigning it. Required
when number_type is ALPHANUMERIC; omit for carrier-assigned types and one is
provisioned.

area_codes.description:
The area codes to put this sender in, in your own order of preference, e.g. ["415", "628"]
for the US or ["20"] for London. Omit it and a number is claimed anywhere in the country.
            
Ordered, and the order is the request. The claim tries each code in turn and stops at the
first that yields a number. Nothing sorts the list and a code listed twice is refused.
            
One to fifty entries, each the area code as digits: 415, with the trunk prefix as
020, or with the country's dialing prefix as +1415 (all are stored as the bare code). A
dialing prefix from a different country than country is refused. Each code is checked against
the country's numbering plan: it must start real local or mobile numbers there, so toll-free and
premium ranges, service codes and another country's codes are refused with a reason.
            
LOCAL senders in any country, and US TEN_DLC senders. No other sender type
has a geographic area code, and the list is refused with one rather than accepted and dropped.
            
Honoured exactly or not at all. Ask for 415 and you get a 415 number or you
get none, never a neighbouring code you did not name. A miss leaves the market with no sender yet and
the codes recorded on it, so it is filled when stock appears rather than filled now from somewhere else.
Many countries outside North America require address or business documents before a local number can
be bought, which can delay or prevent the fill.

numbers.description:
The numbers to assign, one entry per area code, e.g.
[{"area_code": "212", "quantity": 2}, {"area_code": "415"}, {"quantity": 1}]: two numbers in 212,
one in 415 and one in any area code. quantity defaults to 1, and an entry without
area_code means any area code. Omit numbers for one number.
            
Only with LOCAL or TEN_DLC, and not together with area_codes. Each area code is
validated against country the same way area_codes is and may appear once, and at most one
entry may leave area_code out. US TEN_DLC numbers are assigned when the campaign is
approved, not at request time. Not available when the profile inherits the organization's
campaign.

SentDmServicesCommonSenderProfilesContra.description:
One entry of numbers: how many numbers to assign in one area code, or in any area code when
AreaCode is omitted.

area_code.description:
The area code, e.g. 212, validated against the request's country. Omit it for numbers in any
area code.

quantity.description: How many numbers. At least 1; omitted means 1.

SentDmServicesEndpointsCustomerAPIv3Send.description:
The profile's own WhatsApp Business Account, named by the two identifiers the organization cannot answer
for you.
            
No mode: a profile's WABA is its own or it has none. Sharing the organization's would mean
sharing its inbox and its throughput, which makes the two indistinguishable to a recipient — so
inheriting is not offered rather than refused.
            
Everything derivable is derived. Whenever this block is present, the solution the account
arrived through, the client business portfolio that owns it, the access token and that token's expiry are
all resolved from the organization by
IPartnerSolutionService.ResolveAccountCredentialsAsync — the first two off the org's shared-account
listing, the token minted against the org's own solution. They were previously asked for and are no
longer accepted: solution_id and owner_business_id are Meta's answer about provenance, so
taking them from the caller let a request assert a partnership Meta disagreed with, and the listing has to
be consulted regardless because it is what proves the account is one this organization may reach.
            
No access token, and there never was one here: it is minted per client business portfolio and
rotates roughly every sixty days, so a pasted value would be stale before it was useful. Asking a
customer to mint a System User token in Meta Business Manager is skilled work in a console they were
never meant to see, and it would say nothing about which solution the account came from or when it is
revoked.

waba_id.description:
WhatsApp Business Account id — one of the accounts shared into your organization. Required: the
organization holds one per client, and nothing but the caller says which belongs to this profile.

phone_number_id.description:
The Meta phone-number id this profile sends from. Must already be registered under
WabaId.
            
Optional. Omit it to attach the account now and settle the number later: the channel reads as
ACTION_NEEDED with CHANNEL_007, and the profile's WhatsApp messages fail until a number
is named. They do not fall back to the organization's account. Nothing picks one on your behalf.

SentDmServicesEndpointsCustomerAPIv3Send.description:
Asks for an RCS agent of the profile's own, optionally with the full order form inline.
            
Two modes, distinguished by whether any field is populated:
"rcs": {} — intent only. Records that the profile wants its own agent; the order form is
submitted separately through POST /v3/channels/rcs once the fields are ready.
"rcs": { ...fields... } — full form. All required fields must be present; the agent is
created alongside the profile in one call. Omitting opt_in_screenshot_url is allowed.

opt_in_screenshot_url.description: Optional — uploaded separately and its URL may not be known at submission time.

allOf.title: SentDmServicesEndpointsCustomerAPIv3SenderProfilesRequestsPatchSenderProfileRequest_Properties
allOf.description:
Changes a sender profile's own attributes.
            
Only the profile's own attributes. Its identity, its markets and its compliance each get a
sub-resource of their own; accepting them here as well would give every one of those fields two writers
with different validation, and no way to say which won.
            
Every field is optional, and an omitted field is left alone. An explicit null clears the
field — the two are different requests, and SuppliedFields is how the endpoint tells them
apart, because a nullable property cannot.

sending_phone_number_profile_id.description:
Deprecated. Always null. Sender borrowing is gone: a profile no longer points at another

changes the response's shape — a generated client loses the property and stops compiling on the next
regenerate, for a value that is now null for every profile in existence. Keeping it null costs a key and
breaks nobody, and null is the honest answer rather than a placeholder: there is no borrowing left to

- "profile": the profile is billed independently; billing_contact is required.
- "profile_and_organization": the profile is billed first with the organization as fallback; billing_contact is required.

Identifies who receives invoices and who is responsible for payment.

Direct WhatsApp Business Account credentials for this profile.
When provided, the profile uses its own WhatsApp Business Account instead of inheriting from the organization.
When omitted, the profile inherits the organization's WhatsApp Business Account (requires the organization
to have completed WhatsApp Embedded Signup).

allow_contact_sharing.description:
Deprecated. Accepted and ignored. Contact and template sharing between sender profiles is gone
— a profile sees only what it owns, and the organization still sees all of its profiles' contacts and
templates through read-time widening. The four columns behind these flags were dropped by
M260720120000.
            
Bound rather than dropped so the properties survive on the wire and in a generated client: an
SDK that assigns them keeps compiling, which is the compatibility this exists for. Deliberately not
refused either — a 400 would break an integration that is otherwise working, and the capability
they ask for is gone either way. Same rule as SendingPhoneNumberProfileId.
            
The read is what makes this survivable: every profile reports all four as false, so a
caller that checks its own write can see it did not take. Requests carrying one are logged, so we can
tell when nobody sends them any more and the fields can go for real.

sending_phone_number_profile_id.description:
Deprecated. Accepted and ignored. Sender borrowing is gone: a profile cannot send from another
profile's SMS number. Supplying this changes nothing and the request still succeeds.
            
Bound rather than dropped so the property survives on the wire and in a generated client — an SDK
that assigns it keeps compiling, which is the compatibility this exists for. It is deliberately not
refused: a 400 here would break an integration that is otherwise working, and the capability it
asks for is gone either way.
            
The trade-off, stated plainly. A caller asking for borrowing is told it succeeded when
nothing happened. What makes that survivable is the read: sending_phone_number_profile_id comes
back null on every profile, so a caller that checks its own write can see it did not take. Every
request that carries one is logged, so we can tell when nobody is sending it any more and the field can
go for real.
            
Give the profile a sender of its own instead: POST /v3/channels/sms with the
x-profile-id header naming it.
sending_phone_number_profile_id.x-deprecatedMessage: Sender borrowing is gone. Accepted and ignored; supply a sender of the profile's own with POST /v3/channels/sms and the x-profile-id header.

sending_whatsapp_number_profile_id.x-deprecatedMessage: Sender borrowing is gone. Accepted and ignored; supply a sender of the profile's own with POST /v3/channels/whatsapp and the x-profile-id header.

allow_contact_sharing.description:
Deprecated. Accepted and ignored. Contact and template sharing between sender profiles is gone
— a profile sees only what it owns, and the organization still sees all of its profiles' contacts and
templates through read-time widening. The four columns behind these flags were dropped by
M260720120000.
            
Retired the same way as SendingPhoneNumberProfileId, and for the same reason: the
properties stay bound so an SDK that assigns them keeps compiling, and a 400 would break a
working integration over a capability that is gone regardless. Every profile reports all four as
false, so a caller that checks its own write can see it did not take.
allow_contact_sharing.x-deprecatedMessage: Contact and template sharing is gone. Accepted and ignored; every profile reads back false.

allow_template_sharing.x-deprecatedMessage: Contact and template sharing is gone. Accepted and ignored; every profile reads back false.

inherit_contacts.x-deprecatedMessage: Contact inheritance is gone. Accepted and ignored; every profile reads back false.

inherit_templates.x-deprecatedMessage: Template inheritance is gone. Accepted and ignored; every profile reads back false.

allOf.title: SentDmServicesEndpointsCustomerAPIv3MessagesResponsesCancelMessageV3Response_Properties
allOf.description:
The cancelled message, in the shape GET /v3/messages/{id} reports it: a cancellation answers with
the message it acted on rather than a bespoke acknowledgement, so a client can hand the body to the same
reader it already has. status is read off the row the claim just wrote, not asserted by the
endpoint.
            
It carries scheduled_at for the same reason ScheduledMessageResponse does, and
with the same meaning — the instant the message was being held for. A cancelled message was necessarily
held, so the key is present on every real cancellation, and the two endpoints agree on what they report
about the same message. It is a property here rather than inheritance because
ScheduledMessageResponse is sealed.

scheduled_at.description:
The send time that was called off, in UTC — the scheduled_at the message was being
            held for, whether you set it or the recipient's quiet hours moved it there. Omitted only for a held
            message that carried no recorded instant.

SentDmServicesEndpointsCustomerAPIv3Mess.description:
Message response for v3 API — same shape as v2 with snake_case JSON conventions.
            
The shape of a message that was sent immediately: it never has a scheduled_at key. A message that is
or was held for a later instant is a ScheduledMessageResponse, and the endpoint decides which of
the two to answer with. From
always returns this type.

reason_code.description:
Why the message is at its current status, as a stable platform code such as
DELIVERY_007, BUSINESS_003 or
DELIVERY_003. Present when the current status is FAILED, FILTERED or
BLOCKED and the lifecycle was loaded; omitted otherwise. Switch on this rather than on
reason: the code is stable, the wording may be improved. It is the platform's
classification of the outcome, never a carrier or vendor code.

reason.description:
A human-readable sentence for reason_code, for example "Insufficient balance". Omitted whenever
reason_code is.

SentDmServicesCommonEntitiesMessageBody.description:
Structured message body format for database storage.
Preserves channel-specific components (header, header media, body, footer, buttons, MMS subject
and media).
            
Persisted as the messageBody jsonb column on Messages. Every write path goes
through MessageUtils.MessageBodyJsonOptions, which writes nulls, so the envelope shape is
stable regardless of channel or status. Anything that rebuilds this object field by field — the
four IMessageBodyStrategy implementations and MessageUtils.BuildSegmentBody — has to
carry every member, or that member is silently dropped on whichever path forgot it.

subject.description: MMS subject line. Null on every other channel.

media.description:
MMS attachments, as the publicly fetchable URLs handed to the carrier. Null on every other
channel.
            
Persisted rather than derived because a resend and a curfew release rebuild the send from
the stored row — MessageReplayCommandBuilder reads templateId and
templateVariables and nothing else — so media that lives only on the original request
would silently turn a replayed MMS into a text message.

headerMedia.description:
The asset delivered on a media header, when the template has one.
            
Deliberately a separate field rather than part of Header: that is rendered
*text* which RcsChannelOrchestrator prepends as a line of the body, so putting a URL
there would leak a raw link into RCS and SMS transcripts. Keeping the asset out of the text
means display surfaces can show the image while every text path stays clean.

SentDmServicesCommonEntitiesMessageMedia.description:
One attachment on a message, in either direction — and in both, a URL somebody else hosts.
            
Outbound: the customer supplied a public URL and we handed it to the carrier.
Inbound: the carrier hosts the file and we record where. sent.dm never holds the bytes, so
there is no key, no expiry bookkeeping and nothing minted per read — what is stored is what is
served.
            
An inbound link expires on the carrier's own schedule and is unauthenticated. That is the
customer's to manage, and it is documented where they will see it rather than only here — a
recipient who needs an attachment to outlive that window copies it on receipt.
            
Storing a presigned URL is the specific mistake this shape still avoids:
M260826130000 and M260826140000 exist because RCS assets were stored as signed URLs
and went stale. Nothing here is signed.

url.description:
Where the file lives. Outbound: the URL the customer gave us and the carrier fetched. Inbound:
the URL the carrier hosts it at, relayed unchanged.

mediaType.description:
One of MmsMediaTypes when the content type is known. Advisory — a reader should
            trust the fetched object's own Content-Type.

mimeType.description: Content type as the provider declared it. Null when it declared none.

sizeBytes.description: Size as the provider declared it. Never measured here — nothing downloads the file.

sourceHashSha256.description:
Inbound only: the SHA-256 the provider declared alongside the attachment, when it declared one.
Relayed to the customer so they can verify what they fetch matches what the carrier said it sent.
It is the only integrity signal available on an attachment nobody here has read.

SentDmServicesCommonEntitiesMessageHeade.description: The media asset that rode a message's header, recorded as sent.

type.description: "image", "video" or "document" — taken from the header's media variable.

url.description:
The https URL the caller supplied for this send. Never the template's stored
props.sample, which is Meta's expiring header_handle rather than what was delivered.

SentDmServicesEndpointsCustomerAPIv3Mess.description:
A single message activity event for v3 API.
            
The activity list mixes statuses, so unlike a message it is one shape rather than two: a SCHEDULED
entry carries scheduled_at, and every other entry has no such key.

status.description:
Activity status. Outbound: QUEUED, PROCESSED, ROUTED, SCHEDULED, SENT, DELIVERED, READ, FAILED.
Inbound (from contact): RECEIVED (terminal).

from.description: Sender phone number for this activity (the customer's sending number for outbound, the external sender for inbound). Null when not reported by the provider.

scheduled_at.description:
SCHEDULED and CANCELLED activities only, in UTC: on a SCHEDULED entry, when the held
message will be released for delivery; on a CANCELLED entry, the instant that was called off. Same
wire name as on the send response, the message and the webhook. Omitted on every other activity. A message
that quiet hours moved at release has two SCHEDULED entries, each carrying the instant as it stood at
that moment.

reason_code.description:
Why the message reached this status, as a stable platform code such as DELIVERY_007
or BUSINESS_003. Present on FAILED, FILTERED and BLOCKED activities;
omitted on every status that needs no explanation. Switch on this rather than on reason: the code
is stable, the wording may be improved. Same wire name and vocabulary as on the message and the webhook.

Omitted whenever reason_code is.

SentDmServicesEndpointsCustomerAPIv3Mess.description:
The result of a multi-recipient send.
            
Declared here rather than in the service layer. POST /v3/messages used to publish
MessageSendResult — a type in Common.Services.Messaging.Contracts — so the public contract was
whatever the send service happened to return, and changing that service for an internal reason changed the
API. The service keeps its result; this is what a caller sees, and the mapping between them is a decision the
endpoint makes.
            
The shape of an immediate send: it never has a scheduled_at key. A send that carried
scheduled_at is a ScheduledSendMessageResponse, and the endpoint decides which of the two to
answer with. From always returns this type.

status.description:
QUEUED: the batch is accepted. A request that carried scheduled_at is QUEUED
            here too; each message moves to SCHEDULED once it is held, as GET /v3/messages/{id} and the
            message.scheduled webhook report.

SentDmServicesEndpointsCustomerAPIv3Mess.description: What one recipient of a send got, as the API reports it.

message_id.description: Identifier for tracking this recipient's message.

channel.description: Channel this message will be sent on — sms, whatsapp — or null to auto-detect.

body.description: Resolved template body for this recipient's channel, or null when the channel is auto-detected.

allOf.title: SentDmServicesEndpointsCustomerAPIv3MessagesRequestsSendMessageV3Request_Properties
allOf.description: Request to send a message (v3 SDK-style with multi-recipient and multi-channel broadcast)

to.description: List of recipient phone numbers in E.164 format (multi-recipient fan-out)

channel.description:
Channels to broadcast on, e.g. ["whatsapp", "sms"].
Each channel produces a separate message per recipient.
"sent" = auto-detect.
Defaults to ["sent"] (auto-detect) if omitted.

channels.description:
Which of your own numbers to send from, keyed by channel, each channel holding a list of entries:
{"sms": [{"country": "US", "from": ["+12125550000", "+14155550000"]}, {"from": ["+447700800001"]}]}.
Any real channel may be a key; sent, which is auto-detect rather than a channel, is rejected.
country and strategy are accepted and stored but not acted on yet: every entry's
numbers apply to every recipient on that channel.
            
This does not choose channels — Channel does, and the two combine:
"channel": ["sms"] with an sms list sends on SMS from those numbers. Each list only
narrows which of its own channel's routes may win, so with Channel left at
auto-detect a recipient best served by a channel with no list still goes out on it. Routing itself
is unchanged: the same rules are scored and ranked the same way, with routes pinned to numbers you
did not list removed from the running.
            
Each channel's list is independent: an sms list does not restrict MMS. To choose the
numbers a message may go out from as MMS, name them under mms. MMS sends from your SMS numbers, so
an mms list may name any of your active SMS numbers whose market carries MMS — the ones listed under
mms in your channels.
            
Every number must be an active sender on your account. The request itself is still
accepted (202) if one is not — like every other send-time rule, that is decided per message, so
each affected message is recorded BLOCKED with error code BUSINESS_029 and reported on
GET /v3/messages and the status webhook.

template.description:
Template reference (by id or name, with optional parameters).
Optional — provide either Template or Message.

text.description: Plain-text (free-form) message body. Provide either Template or this.

media_urls.description:
Attachments for this send, as publicly fetchable https URLs. Used by the MMS channel and ignored
by every other one.
            
Supplying these replaces the media on the template's mms body rather than
adding to it, so a template can hold a default creative while a caller still sends something
recipient-specific.
            
Their presence is also what makes a message eligible for MMS on an auto-detect send: a
message with nothing attached is delivered as SMS, because an MMS with no media is a more
expensive text message. For the same reason a send that names mms in channel with
nothing attached, here or on the template, is refused with a 400.
            
The recipient's carrier fetches each URL after the send is accepted, so it must stay
publicly reachable — a link that expires, or one behind auth, arrives as a failed message.

subject.description:
Subject line for this send, overriding the template's. MMS only; ignored on every other channel.
Most handsets render it above the body, some ignore it entirely.

scheduled_at.description:
Optional future send time as an ISO-8601 timestamp with an explicit UTC offset, e.g.
2026-10-01T09:00:00+02:00 or 2026-10-01T07:00:00Z. A value without an offset is rejected
(400) rather than read in the server's zone. The offset only fixes the instant: it is stored and echoed
in UTC as scheduled_at. Omit to send now. Must be at least one minute ahead and at most 30 days
ahead. Accepted messages report SCHEDULED and are released for delivery at this time. Quiet hours,
balance and template approval are evaluated at release, not at acceptance: a message whose time
falls inside a recipient's protected quiet-hours window is moved to the next allowed time and a second
message.scheduled webhook reports the new scheduled_at.

SentDmServicesEndpointsCustomerAPIv3Mess.description:
One entry of a channel's list in Channels, e.g.
{"country": "US", "from": ["+15559990002", "+15559990003"], "strategy": "sticky"}.

country.description:
Recipient country this entry is meant for (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. US). Optional. Accepted
and stored, not acted on yet.

from.description:
Sender numbers in E.164. Each must be an active sender on your account for this channel. That is
account state rather than request shape, so it is decided per message: the request is accepted
with 202 and a message naming an unusable number is recorded BLOCKED with error code
BUSINESS_029.

strategy.description:
How to pick a number from From, e.g. sticky or geo. Optional. Accepted
and stored, not acted on yet.

SentDmServicesCommonServicesTemplatesCon.description: SDK-style template reference: resolve by ID or by name, with optional parameters.

parameters.description:
Template variable parameters for personalization, keyed by variable name.
            
Every variable the template declares is required; GET /v3/templates/{id} lists them.
Supplying a key the template does not declare is ignored.
            
Media headers. A template whose header is an image (designed in WhatsApp Manager and
imported into Sent) declares a reserved header_image key. Its value is a publicly
reachable https URL that Meta fetches at send time — Sent does not host the asset, and the
sample approved with the template is not reused. The key is derived from the header's media type,
so header_video and header_document follow the same shape when those formats ship.
            
"parameters": {
  "header_image": "https://cdn.example.com/banner.jpg",
  "name": "John Doe"
}

SentDmServicesEndpointsCustomerAPIv3Comp.description: Everything a market expects of a sender, for one channel, country and sender type.

channel.description:
Channel the requirements apply to — sms, whatsapp or rcs.
            
Echoed so the document says which channel it describes. It always described one: setup's
last step is a specific channel path, and every type is an SMS sender type — but a caller reading
the payload had to infer that from the path to know it.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country the requirements apply to.

type.description:
Sender type the requirements apply to.
            
Non-nullable while sms is the only channel answered here, because it is the only channel
whose senders have a type — the day another one is answered, this becomes nullable along with it. Not
nullable in advance: nothing can emit null today, and publishing a shape the API never sends is the
same mistake as publishing a field it does not have.

required.description:
Whether this market demands anything before a sender can be registered. When false, the
compliance array may be omitted entirely and the profile is ready once provisioned.

sender_id_pattern.description:
Pattern the sender's own value must match, where the market dictates one — alphanumeric
sender ids and short codes. Null when the value is carrier-assigned.

requirements.description:
Values to supply in compliance. Empty when the market demands nothing. Values Sent
supplies on your behalf are never listed, and neither are ones it derives from what you send.

setup.description:
The calls that set this market up, in the order they have to be made, each carrying a body that can be
sent as it stands.
            
This is the answer to "what do I actually do". Requirements describes each value
the market wants; this assembles those descriptions into the requests that supply them, so a caller — or an
agent acting for one — copies a body out and sends it rather than building one from a table.
            
The last step is always the channel itself, and it is where the regime's own values are supplied.
The one before it, where there is one, is the brand a registering market files against — so it is a step of
its own and the channel call refuses until it exists. A market that registers with nobody has one step.

SentDmServicesEndpointsCustomerAPIv3Comp.description: One value a market expects in a channel call's compliance map.

key.description: Key to use in the compliance map.

type.description:
Value type: string, number, boolean, date, enum,
object, array or document.

format.description:
Refinement of type where the market demands a specific shape, e.g. e164,
url, email, iso3166_alpha2, csv_keywords.

required.description: Whether the market always demands this value.

required_when.description:
Condition that makes this value required, when it is only required in some cases —
e.g. brand.entity_type == PUBLIC_PROFIT. Evaluate it against your own payload to know
whether to collect the field.

options.description: Accepted values, when the type is an enum or a constrained array.

min_length.description:
Shortest acceptable value, where the market sets one. TCR refuses a consent narrative under 40
characters, and finding that out at submission time is the round trip this exists to save.

max_items.description: Most entries this value accepts, where the market caps it.

item_fields.description:
Shape of each entry, when this requirement is a list of objects rather than of scalars.
            
The compliance value stays null in the setup body like every other blank —
a body that carries a half-filled object is one the endpoint refuses, which would break the promise
that the published body can be sent as it stands. So the shape is described here instead, and each
entry the caller composes has these keys.

label.description: Human label, suitable for a form field.

notes.description: Why the market asks for this.

SentDmServicesEndpointsCustomerAPIv3Comp.description:
One call to make, with a body that can be sent as it stands.
            
The steps are ordered and the order is load-bearing: a channel that registers with a regime is filed
against a brand, so the brand call comes first and the channel call refuses until it has been made. Doing them
in order is the whole of setting a market up.

step.description: Position in the sequence, from 1. Steps must be performed in this order.

resource.description: What this call sets up: brand or channel.

path.description:

allOf.title: SentDmServicesEndpointsCustomerAPIv3ChannelsRequestsAddSmsChannelRequest_Properties
allOf.description:
Adds an SMS market — a country and a sender type — to a customer.
            
The same fields channels.sms takes on POST /v3/sender-profiles, because it is the same
work: create is "make the profile, then add its first market", and both run one provisioning path.
compliance is top-level and answers for the market this request concerns, exactly as it does
there.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country the sender operates in.

number_type.description:
Sender type. Decides the provisioning flow and what compliance is asked for.
            
[Required] so the published document says so. The validator has always demanded it, but
requiredness reached the schema by matching a rule to a property name — which works for country,
whose wire name is its camel-cased C# name, and silently does not for number_type. A client
generating a request from our OpenAPI therefore sent what the document called sufficient and was
answered 400.
x-enum-descriptions: A geographic number for the country. The ordinary choice: recognisable to recipients, and available almost everywhere.
A toll-free number. High throughput and no per-country registration, but US toll-free traffic goes through its own verification.
A short code — five or six digits, leased rather than provisioned. Highest throughput, longest lead time, and the most expensive.
A sender name rather than a number, up to 11 characters. Recipients cannot reply. Not available in every country, and several require it to be pre-registered with documents.

A US 10-digit long code registered with The Campaign Registry. The only sender type that registers with a compliance regime, so it is the only one whose market declares `compliance.brand` and `compliance.campaign`.
A mobile number. Where a country distinguishes it from a landline, some carriers treat mobile traffic differently.
The industry's spelling of `TEN_DLC`, accepted so an integrator can send the term it knows. Resolves to the same market.

sender_value.description:
The sender's identity where the caller chooses it. Required when number_type is
ALPHANUMERIC; optional for carrier-assigned types, which are procured afterwards.

area_codes.description:
The area codes to put this sender in, in your own order of preference, e.g. ["415", "628"]
for the US or ["20"] for London. Omit it and a number is claimed anywhere in the country.
            
Ordered, and the order is the request. The claim tries each code in turn and stops at the
first that yields a number. Nothing sorts the list and a code listed twice is refused.
            
One to fifty entries, each the area code as digits: 415, with the trunk prefix as
020, or with the country's dialing prefix as +1415 (all are stored as the bare code). A
dialing prefix from a different country than country is refused. Each code is checked against
the country's numbering plan: it must start real local or mobile numbers there, so toll-free and
premium ranges, service codes and another country's codes are refused with a reason.
            
LOCAL senders in any country, and US TEN_DLC senders. No other sender type
has a geographic area code, and the list is refused with one rather than accepted and dropped.
            
Honoured exactly or not at all. Ask for 415 and you get a 415 number or you
get none, never a neighbouring code you did not name. A miss leaves the market with no sender yet and
the codes recorded on it, so it is filled when stock appears rather than filled now from somewhere else.
Many countries outside North America require address or business documents before a local number can
be bought, which can delay or prevent the fill.

numbers.description:
The numbers to assign, one entry per area code, e.g.
[{"area_code": "212", "quantity": 2}, {"area_code": "415"}, {"quantity": 1}]: two numbers in 212,
one in 415 and one in any area code. quantity defaults to 1, and an entry without
area_code means any area code. Omit numbers for one number.
            
Only with LOCAL or TEN_DLC, and not together with area_codes. Each area code is
validated against country the same way area_codes is and may appear once, and at most one
entry may leave area_code out. On a LOCAL market you already hold, this adds the numbers to
it. US TEN_DLC numbers are assigned when the campaign is approved, not at request time. Not
available when the profile inherits the organization's campaign.

compliance.description:
What this market registers with. Its members are declared by the market itself — call `GET /v3/compliance/requirements?country=&type=` for the authoritative set.

**US `TEN_DLC` is the only market that registers with a regime**, and the only one whose compliance carries `brand` and `campaign`; those are the members described here. Every other market's compliance is document keys, which come from configuration rather than from code and so cannot be listed in this document.

allOf.title: SentDmServicesEndpointsCustomerAPIv3ChannelsRequestsAddVoiceChannelRequest_Properties
allOf.description:
Turns phone calls on for a number: one you already hold, or a new one.
            
Voice is per number the way SMS is per market: each number you hold can carry calls on its own,
and each has its own callback URL, where Sent asks what to do with every call on it, or a voice agent
that answers calls to it. The first number you turn voice on for becomes the line app-originated calls
are placed from when a voice token names no number.
            
Send number to add calls to a number you already hold, or leave it out to be given a new
US number — optionally in a particular area_code. The two are alternatives, not a pair.

number.description:
One of your phone numbers, in E.164 format. Leave the field out entirely to be given a new one
instead; sending it empty is a refused request rather than a request for a new number.

area_code.description:
The US area code a new number should be in, as 212. Only for a request that leaves
number out — sending both says two different things about which number to use, and is
refused. Omit it too and the number comes from anywhere in the country.

callback_url.description:
Where Sent asks what to do with each call on this number: an absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL on a public
host. A signed question is POSTed here when a call arrives or a caller presses a key, and the answer
decides the call. Every question is signed with the callback_secret the response returns, the
same way your webhooks are signed. Turning the number on again with a different URL replaces it and
keeps the secret. Required unless agent_id is sent.

agent_id.description:
One of your voice agents (GET /v3/voice/agents), such as
agent_9f2ab000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001, to answer calls to this number. It wins over
callback_url for calls to the number, and both may be sent; calls your app places from the
number still follow your app. Send it instead of callback_url for a number only an agent answers.

default_for_app_calls.description:
Make this the line app-originated calls are placed from when a voice token names no number.
Omit it and your first voice number takes that role; a later one leaves it where it is.

allOf.title: SentDmServicesEndpointsCustomerAPIv3ChannelsMarketComplianceWriteRequest_Properties
allOf.description:
Amends what a market declares for compliance.
            
The body is the market's, wrapped in compliance — the same wrapper
POST /v3/channels/sms takes and the same one GET on this path returns, so what comes back can
be sent back unchanged. There is no brand or campaign in the path to make the wrapper
redundant: both halves are singletons of the market, and both are written here.
            
Partial, at every level. An omitted key is left alone and an explicit null clears it —
which is what PATCH means, and why this is not a PUT. A body naming nothing is refused rather
than silently accepted, and a nullable value cannot tell "not sent" from "sent as null", so the binder
records which names the body carried.
            
Nothing here creates a second anything. Both halves are one slot, so a write is an upsert and
a replayed request lands on the row it already wrote. That is what makes this safe to sit behind a verb
clients auto-retry — a collection would have put a paid TCR filing there instead.

Account response for GET /v3/me endpoint.

sending_phone_number.description:

no US SMS sender.
            
The same value as channels.sms.phone_number, published under both names on purpose:
sending_phone_number is what this value is already called on GET /v3/profiles, so the
same key answers the same question whichever of the two endpoints you ask. Neither name is preferred
over the other and neither is deprecated.
            
The same value, not the same presence: this key is always written, including as null,
whereas channels.sms.phone_number is left out entirely when there is no sender.

The account that holds sending_phone_number in number inventory: normally this account
itself, and a different account when the number is held elsewhere. Null when there is no US

Whether this account may mark a template for automatic creation on its sender profiles. Granted by
Sent per account and off by default, so it is what a template-create form reads to decide whether to
offer the option at all — marking a template without it does nothing.
            
Top-level rather than inside settings, which is written for type: "profile" only
and so would never carry it to the account type that can act on it.
            
This is the capability, not the stored flag: a profile reports false whatever its
own row holds. A sender profile owns no sender profiles, so a template it marked would have nothing
to be created on and the fan-out would never read the flag. The admin GET /customers/{id}
reports the stored value instead, because that is the one an operator granted.

phone_number.description: RCS-enabled phone number in E.164 format

allow_contact_sharing.description:
Always false. A profile no longer shares contacts with sibling profiles — it sees only what
it owns. Retained so existing v3 clients reading allow_contact_sharing keep deserializing; it
carries no information.
allow_contact_sharing.x-deprecatedMessage: Always false. Sender profiles no longer share contacts; the flag it reported is gone.

allow_template_sharing.description:
Always false. A profile no longer shares templates with sibling profiles. Retained so
existing v3 clients reading allow_template_sharing keep deserializing; it carries no
information.
allow_template_sharing.x-deprecatedMessage: Always false. Sender profiles no longer share templates; the flag it reported is gone.

inherit_contacts.description:
Always false. A profile no longer inherits its organization's contacts. Retained so existing
v3 clients reading inherit_contacts keep deserializing; it carries no information.
inherit_contacts.x-deprecatedMessage: Always false. Sender profiles no longer inherit contacts; the flag it reported is gone.

inherit_templates.description:
Always false. A profile no longer inherits its organization's templates. Retained so existing
v3 clients reading inherit_templates keep deserializing; it carries no information.
inherit_templates.x-deprecatedMessage: Always false. Sender profiles no longer inherit templates; the flag it reported is gone.

inherit_tcr_brand.description: Whether this profile inherits TCR brand from the organization

inherit_tcr_campaign.description: Whether this profile inherits TCR campaign from the organization

billing_model.description: Billing model: profile, organization, or profile_and_organization

SentDmServicesEndpointsCustomerAPIv3Acco.description: Profile (sender profile) response for v3 API

role.description: User's role in this profile: admin, billing, developer (inherited from organization if not explicitly set)

status.description: Profile setup status: incomplete, pending_review, approved, rejected

SentDmServicesCommonServicesWebhooksCont.description:
The envelope Sent POSTs to a subscribed webhook endpoint. Every event shares this shape and
varies only in Payload.

field.description:
The event family, for example message, templates or contact. Route on
this first, then on event for the specific change.

event.description:
The specific event within the family, for example message.delivered,
message.received or contact.opt_out. Absent on events that have no subtype, so
treat it as optional.

timestamp.description:
When Sent emitted the event, in UTC (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ). This is the emission
time, not the time the underlying change happened. Use the timestamp inside the payload for
the latter.

SentDmServicesCommonServicesWebhooksCont.description:
Body of an outbound message lifecycle event. Delivered once per status change, so a single
message produces several of these as it moves toward a terminal status.

updated_at.description:
When the message reached the status this event reports, in UTC
(yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ).

account_id.description: The account the message belongs to.

message_id.description:
The message this event describes. Stable across every event in the message's lifecycle, so
use it to correlate them.

template_id.description: The template the message was sent from, when it was sent from one.

template_name.description:
Name of the template the message was sent from. Omitted when the message wasn't
template-based.

outbound_number.description: The recipient's number in E.164 format.

agent_id.description: The agent attributed to the send, when the send was attributed to one.

message_status.description:
The status the message just reached, for example SENT, DELIVERED, or
FAILED. Sent means dispatched and delivered means confirmed, so treat them as
distinct outcomes.

channel.description:
The channel the message went out on, for example sms or whatsapp. A message
that falls back to another channel reports the channel actually used.

body.description:
The rendered message body, as plain text. Sent as null when we aren't asserting a
body for this event. The field is always present, so read it and check for null rather than
checking whether the key exists. Truncated to 3072 characters.

scheduled_at.description:
message.scheduled and message.cancelled only, in UTC (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ): on
message.scheduled it is when the held message will be released for delivery, on
message.cancelled the release instant that was called off — the same instant, before and after.
A consumer that recorded a future send from the first event has what it needs to un-record it from the
second. Omitted on every other event.

schedule_reason.description:
message.scheduled only: why the message is held, either because you scheduled it or because
the recipient is inside a protected quiet-hours window. Omitted on every other event, including
message.cancelled — that is a property of the hold, not of the cancellation, and repeating it
there would read as "why was this cancelled", which it does not answer.

reason_code.description:
Why the message reached this status, as a stable platform code such as
DELIVERY_007 or BUSINESS_003. Present on
message.failed, message.filtered and message.blocked; omitted on every status that
needs no explanation. Switch on this rather than on Reason: the code is
stable, the wording may be improved. It is the platform's classification of the outcome and never a
carrier or vendor code.

reason.description:
A human-readable sentence for ReasonCode, for example "The recipient is not registered on
this channel". Omitted whenever reason_code is.

field.description:
